nodes.description: Homozygous missense variants in GEMIN4 initiate the disorder. Structural modelling places the three reported substitutions in the helical scaffold of the protein, where they are predicted to destabilise the fold and may impair the accessibility of a nuclear localisation signal. That the variants reduce rather than abolish GEMIN4 function is an inference: complete loss of Gemin4 is embryonic lethal in mice, whereas patients survive into childhood. No study has measured GEMIN4 protein abundance or SMN complex composition in patient cells.

nodes.description: GEMIN4 is a component of the SMN complex, binding it through a direct interaction with Gemin3 and contacting several Sm proteins, and is required for efficient assembly of the Sm core onto spliceosomal snRNAs. Reduced snRNP assembly is the best-supported cellular function of GEMIN4, but it has not been demonstrated in NEDMCR patient cells, and no downstream splicing defect has been linked to any NEDMCR phenotype. The node is therefore not connected to phenotypes; see the nedmcr_smn_complex_link discussion.
